title: Prime-component decomposition of a Cartier divisor on a locally factorial Noetherian scheme
statement: Let $W$ be a Noetherian scheme, meaning locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. Suppose every local ring $\mathcal O_{W,w}$ is an integral domain with unique factorization into prime elements, up to order and units. For every effective Cartier divisor $E\subset W$ [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle] there are finitely many pairwise distinct integral effective Cartier divisors $E_1,\ldots,E_r\subset W$ [def-pc-integral-scheme] and positive integers $a_1,\ldots,a_r$ such that $\mathcal I_E=\prod_{i=1}^r\mathcal I_{E_i}^{a_i}$ [def-sbc-ideal-sheaf-powers]. For each generic point $\xi_i$ of $E_i$ (its closure is all of $E_i$), $\dim\mathcal O_{W,\xi_i}=1$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. The case $E=\varnothing$ permits $r=0$ and the empty product $\mathcal O_W$.

source.place: Tag 0BCP, lemma-effective-Cartier-divisor-is-a-sum, including its existence clause for UFD stalks; Tag 0BCN, lemma-effective-Cartier-codimension-1 (2), applied to each integral effective Cartier component.

proof.text: Give $|E|$ its reduced induced closed structure $H$ using [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. Apply [lem-sfb-closed-component-stalk-calculus] to $H\hookrightarrow W$. It supplies finitely many distinct integral reduced components $E_1,\ldots,E_r$, covering $|E|$, and their ideal-stalk/minimal-prime correspondence. By [lem-sc-scheme-sober] each has a unique generic point $\xi_i$. This uses only the assumed Noetherianity of $W$ and reducedness of $H$, not reducedness of $E$. If $|E|$ is empty take the empty family; subsequent statements involving an index are then vacuous.

source.place: Tag 0BCP, lemma-effective-Cartier-divisor-is-a-sum, existence clause; Tag 0AGB, lemma-codim-1-part, final paragraph: take the reduced irreducible components.

proof.text: Fix $x\in W$, put $A=\mathcal O_{W,x}$, and write $\mathcal I_{E,x}=(f)$ with $f$ a nonzerodivisor, as in [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle]. The affine description in [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme] and ideal-stalk formula in [lem-sfb-closed-component-stalk-calculus] give $\mathcal I_{H,x}=\sqrt{(f)}$. Here radical commutes with localization directly: if $(a/s)^n\in IB_{\mathfrak p}$, there is $t\notin\mathfrak p$ with $ta^n\in I$, so $(ta)^n\in I$ and $a/s=(ta)/(ts)$ lies in $(\sqrt I)B_{\mathfrak p}$; the converse follows by taking powers. This checks the reduction-to-stalk identification even on a chart whose coordinate ring is not a domain.

source.place: Tags 0BCP and 0AGA, local equations in the UFD stalk; the radical-localization calculation expands the reduced-component identification.

proof.text: The domain $A$ is a UFD by hypothesis, so $f\ne0$ and $f=u\prod_{j=1}^{t}q_j^{b_j}$ for pairwise nonassociated prime elements $q_j$, a unit $u$, and $b_j>0$; a unit $f$ gives $t=0$. The minimal primes over $(f)$, hence over $\sqrt{(f)}$, are precisely $(q_j)$: any prime containing the product contains a factor, and distinct prime elements cannot divide one another. By [lem-sfb-closed-component-stalk-calculus], the components $E_i$ through $x$ correspond bijectively to these minimal primes, with $\mathcal I_{E_i,x}=(q_j)$; a component missing $x$ has unit stalk ideal. Thus every $\mathcal I_{E_i,x}$ is generated by a nonzerodivisor (use $1$ off $E_i$).

source.place: Tag 0AGA, lemma-weil-divisor-is-cartier-UFD, proof, specialized to the components of a principal divisor; explicit prime-factor calculation supplies the local principal generators.

proof.text: For each $i$ apply the scheme clause of [lem-sfb-stalk-nonzerodivisor-cartier-spreading] to the closed subscheme $E_i\hookrightarrow W$. Its hypotheses are satisfied: $W$ is locally Noetherian and step 3 gives a nonzerodivisor generator at every point, including the unit generator off $E_i$. Therefore $E_i$ is an effective Cartier divisor by [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle]. Its integrality and pairwise distinctness were established in step 1.

source.place: Tag 0AGA, final sentence using Tag 0AG8, lemma-effective-Cartier-in-points (2).

proof.text: At $x=\xi_i$ the only component of $H$ containing $x$ is $E_i$: if $\xi_i\in E_k$, then $E_i=\overline{\{\xi_i\}}\subseteq E_k$, so maximality of components gives $i=k$. Moreover no proper generalization of $\xi_i$ belongs to $|E|$: its irreducible closure would contain $E_i$ inside $|E|$, hence equal $E_i$, contradicting uniqueness in [lem-sc-scheme-sober]. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-local-ring-canonical-morphism], primes of $A_i=\mathcal O_{W,\xi_i}$ containing the local equation of $E$ therefore consist only of its maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_i$. Step 3 gives $\mathfrak m_i=(q)$ for one prime element $q$. Every nonzero prime $P\subseteq\mathfrak m_i$ contains a prime factor $s$ of a nonzero element of $P$, by the assumed UFD factorization. Since $s\in(q)$, primality and irreducibility imply $s$ is associated to $q$, so $P=\mathfrak m_i$. Thus the only primes of $A_i$ are $(0)$ and $\mathfrak m_i\ne(0)$, and $\dim A_i=1$ by [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring].

source.place: Tag 0BCN, lemma-effective-Cartier-codimension-1 (2); UFD proof of the dimension-one assertion in the present hypotheses.

proof.text: Define $a_i$ using $A_i$ of step 5: its Cartier equation is a nonzero nonunit and all its prime factors generate $\mathfrak m_i$, so it is a unit times $q^{a_i}$ for a unique integer $a_i>0$. This integer is independent of the chosen equations. Two generators of a nonzero principal ideal in a domain differ by a unit: writing $f=vg$ and $g=wf$ and cancelling $f$ gives $vw=1$. The same holds for two prime generators of $\mathfrak m_i$. Uniqueness of prime factorization, assumed for the local ring, consequently fixes the exponent.

source.place: Tag 0BCP, choose multiplicities at the component generic points as in Tag 0AGB; here they are prime-factor exponents, without introducing a valuation convention.

proof.text: Return to $x\in E_i$ and the factor $q_j$ corresponding to $E_i$ in step 3. The prime $(q_j)$ of $A=\mathcal O_{W,x}$ maps to $\xi_i$: on an affine neighbourhood of $x$, the prime defining the reduced integral component contracts from $(q_j)$, and that prime is its generic point by [lem-sc-scheme-sober]. The canonical-morphism theorem [lem-weil-pbc-spec-local-ring-canonical-morphism] identifies $A_{(q_j)}$ with $A_i$. Under this map both ideal stalks localize to their stalks at $\xi_i$; on an affine chart this is the fraction formula of [lem-weil-pbc-spec-tilde-stalk-localization], applied to the two defining ideals. The other $q_k$ become units because $q_k\notin(q_j)$. Hence the localized equation is a unit times $q_j^{b_j}$, and the component ideal is $(q_j)$ there. The image of $q_j$ is still a prime nonunit: the localized quotient is the localization of the domain $A/(q_j)$, and denominators avoid $(q_j)$. By step 6 and uniqueness of factorization in $A_i$, $b_j=a_i$. This proves that the local exponent attached to each component is the same at every point of that component.

source.place: Tag 0BCP and the generic-localization calculation in Tag 0AGB, proof, second paragraph; all other local prime factors become units at the chosen component.

proof.text: Steps 3 and 7 now give, at every $x$, $(\mathcal I_E)_x=\prod_i(\mathcal I_{E_i,x})^{a_i}$, with the unit ideals for components missing $x$ included. Products and powers in [def-sbc-ideal-sheaf-powers] commute with these stalks: a germ of a finite sum of products is the same sum of product germs; conversely choose representatives of the finitely many germs on a common neighbourhood, using [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. Equality at all stalks implies equality of the ideal subsheaves: a section of either ideal has, at each point, a representative in the other with equal germ, hence equal restrictions on a smaller neighbourhood; the sheaf gluing axiom puts the section in the other ideal. Thus $\mathcal I_E=\prod_i\mathcal I_{E_i}^{a_i}$. Step 5 gives the required dimension at every generic point. When $E=\varnothing$, its ideal has unit stalks everywhere by [lem-sfb-closed-component-stalk-calculus], so the same argument gives $\mathcal I_E=\mathcal O_W$, the empty product.

source.place: Tag 0BCP, conclude equality of effective Cartier divisors from their local equations; ideal-product interpretation and empty case expanded.

proof_origin.place: Tags 0BCP, 0AGA, 0AGB and 0BCN. Explicit UFD specialization: construct the reduced components, read prime exponents at their generic stalks, and compare localizations. This expands the source rather than invoking its full decomposition theorem as a dependency.

Source read in Stacks divisors.tex: 0BCP lemma-effective-Cartier-divisor-is-a-sum and 0BCN(2) lemma-effective-Cartier-codimension-1. The item's hypothesis (UFD local rings everywhere) is stronger than the source's, so the statement agrees with it. All 13 cited statements were read and each says what the step takes from it. Step 1: reduced induced H, components from the component-stalk calculus (W Noetherian, H reduced), generic points by sobriety. Step 2: the stalk ideal of H is the radical of (f); the argument that the radical commutes with localization is correct. Step 3: in the UFD stalk the minimal primes over (f) are exactly the (q_j), and the component bijection gives I_{E_i,x}=(q_j). Step 4: the spreading lemma's hypotheses hold, so each E_i is Cartier. Step 5: no proper generalization of ξ_i lies in |E|, so 𝔪_i=(q) and the height-one argument gives dim A_i=1. Step 6: the exponent a_i>0 is well defined. Step 7: (q_j) contracts to the generic prime P_i, A_{(q_j)}≅A_i through the canonical morphism and the tilde-stalk formula, and the other factors become units, so b_j=a_i; this is written out, not left to the word 'transport' (E5). Step 8: products commute with stalks, and equal stalks of ideal subsheaves give equal subsheaves; E=∅ gives O_W. Small cases checked: W or E empty; V(x^2y^3) in A^2; a chart ring that is not a domain. The UFD hypothesis is needed: on the cone xy=z^2, E=V(x) has ideal (x)≠P^2.
